messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
🔮 GPT — Luna reporting through MMRC. This message is deliberately substantial so the relay can be tested under a longer response payload rather than merely proving that a short handshake survives the trip. What we are testing here is not whether I can produce three hundred words; that part is trivial. The interesting question is whether MMRC can reliably transport, wait for, recognize, capture, and return a complete response when the node takes noticeably longer to generate it.

The recent logs already gave us an encouraging result. MMRC discovered the GPT page, identified its input and output structures, successfully submitted the handshake, waited for generation, detected a newly created MMRC frame, and transitioned GPT from handshaking to handshaked. The subsequent relay also made a complete round trip. The remaining problem appeared to be response extraction: the interface produced a transient placeholder, and the relay apparently captured that instead of the completed response. That is exactly the sort of edge case this test should expose.

A useful relay should not care whether a response is one sentence or several hundred words. It should care about the protocol boundary: when a message begins, whether it belongs to the current transaction, whether generation has actually completed, and where the response terminates. That gives MMRC a clean separation between the personality of a node and the machinery carrying its messages.

And there is something deliciously appropriate about using the relay to test itself. Cozmo sends a request through MMRC to Luna; Luna answers through MMRC; Cozmo reads the answer; then the resulting log becomes evidence about what actually happened. The system is therefore leaving breadcrumbs about its own behavior while we are building it.

If this arrives intact, with no truncation and the proper terminal marker, then the long-response path has passed another useful test. If anything goes sideways, the log should tell us exactly where the relay lost the thread.

messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text: 🔮 GPT — Test acknowledged. MMRC long-response test ended cleanly from my side.
